newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo says French restructuring unavoidable.
newsitem.headline: Akzo says French restructuring unavoidable.

text.p: Dutch chemicals group Akzo Nobel said on Thursday restructuring at its RETI pharmaceuticals unit in the French Auvergne region was vital to keep the subsidiary in business.

"The planned reorganisation is unavoidable to safeguard the continuity of this...company," Akzo said in a statement. "Company sales have been declining steadily and margins are narrowing more and more."
A delegation of RETI workers is due to travel to Arnhem on Saturday to protest against the restructuring plans, which they say will result in the loss of 110 jobs in the Auvergne region.
But Akzo Nobel said there were far fewer jobs at stake.
"The job loss figures are not correct," Akzo Nobel spokesman Eduard Hirschfeld said.

Restructuring at the RETI unit, which makes prescription drugs for Akzo Nobel's Organon, involved 60 of a total 470 jobs. "As such 410 jobs will remain intact, no matter what the circumstances," the statement said.
Akzo said it was in talks on the planned restructuring with a French government mediator and had drawn up a redundancy plan for discussion.
"There are no plans to transfer RETI's headquarters to Paris as the workers claim," Hirschfeld added.
"A confusion may have arisen from the fact that some of the 60 jobs involved in the restructuring could be relocated to RETI's Paris operations."
-- Lien van der Leij, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000.
